title: ADR-0055 and permissions docs: name the authored-policy outcome of the controlled_by_parent predicate-write change (after #36282)
body:
repo:objectstack#4 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5kt9AD1TPLy7Y9oa9D

Filing gate: ② follow-up from a landing PR (PR #36282, card #35802). It carries nits N1 and N5 of contract record 7076369115 (seat 7, PASS at `4fe236dbd1`). Maintainer 2026-11-22 07:49Z 「你后续的小改动可以另立卡。尽快完成合并」. Source: fleet. ⛔ Not a claim. Queued, not dispatched by area a4-E.

## Why

PR #36282's release note declares two narrowed outcomes for a non-delegated predicate update or delete on a `controlled_by_parent` detail:
- all matched rows or none;
- where the app authors an `update`/`delete` row-level policy with a `using` on the detail, that policy alone now bounds the write. The caller's own rows that the policy does not admit are no longer written, which matches by-id.

The governed text and two of the docs pages do not say the second outcome yet.

## Where

- **N1:** `docs/adr/0055-master-detail-controlled-by-parent.md`, the 2026-11-22 amendment.
  - Its "What is unchanged" list still carries "An app-authored row-level policy binds every row".
  - "The declared narrowing" names only the all-or-none outcome.
  - Add one sentence naming the authored-policy outcome, and move or qualify that bullet.
- **N5:** `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx` says a predicate write "writes the rows a by-id write of each would". That leaves out the `ownerMayEdit` owner leg, which still differs in the refusing direction (ruling 7073030861, item 2).
  - `rls.mdx` already states the authored-policy case.
  - `permissions-matrix.mdx` and `sharing-rules.mdx` do not.

## Done when

- The ADR amendment names both narrowed outcomes.
- The three permissions pages agree with each other and with the changeset `.changeset/35802-cbp-predicate-write-master-gate.md`.
- No rule changes: this is wording only.

Land after PR #36282. The ADR is a governed path, so this goes through the contract review at its tier.
